newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen firmer, but rise may slow.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen firmer, but rise may slow.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to retain a firm tone on Tuesday, but buyers may become slightly cautious after five consecutive trading days of gains in the key market index which brought it above 18,500 points for the first time in about a month on Monday, brokers said.
On Monday, the 225-share Nikkei average finished up 199.52 points, or 1.09 percent, at 18,551.66. June Nikkei futures added 180 points to end at 18,580.
"The Nikkei rose through 18,500 yesterday, but it will not be easy for it to rise sharply from this level," said a broker at a second-tier Japanese securities house.

Brokers said lower-priced stocks, such as in the raw-materials sector, where earnings are expected to be stable, would likely lead the market, while the recent buying back in the financial sector should continue to provide relief.
"It might not become a sharp rise today," said a "Big Four" senior broker. "But we want to buy on any dips."
